plate_tectonics.goal: Rock of density ρ lies above you to a depth h, pulled down by gravity g. Write the pressure P it presses on you with.
plate_tectonics.name: Lithostatic pressure
plate_tectonics.ask: Find P in gigapascals 100 km down, with rock of density R = 3300 kg/m³ and g = 9.81 m/s².
plate_tectonics.method: Each layer carries the weight of everything above it: a column of area A and height h weighs ρ·A·h·g.

mantle_geodynamics.goal: A layer of thickness L is heated from below by a temperature difference ΔT. Whether it turns over depends on one number: buoyancy (ρ g α ΔT) against heat diffusion κ and viscosity μ. Write that number, N.
mantle_geodynamics.name: Rayleigh number
mantle_geodynamics.form: ρ * g * α * T * L ^ 3 / ( κ * μ )
mantle_geodynamics.expr: R * g * a * T * H ^ 3 / ( k * m )
mantle_geodynamics.ask: Find N for the whole mantle: R = 4000 kg/m³, a = 3e-5 /K, T = 2500 K, H = 2.9e6 m, k = 1e-6 m²/s, m = 1e22 Pa·s.
mantle_geodynamics.method: Compare how fast a warm blob rises (buoyancy over viscosity) with how fast it loses its heat (diffusion). Above about 1000 the layer convects.
